doc.title: Dianne Reeves interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, October 13, 2001

title: Recording the Sarah Vaughan tribute live in four days
summary: The tribute album was recorded live in four days, with cousin George Duke overseeing the sound and strings who once recorded for Sarah.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Your last album with the Sarah Vaughan tribute, it must have been an amazing feeling to stand in front of that orchestra. It was done mostly all live, is that correct?

Yeah. It was amazing because, well first of all, and I have to brag, my cousin George Duke is an impeccable musician. He’s someone that if he needed to conduct the orchestra he could have done that, if he needed to run the board recording equipment he could have done that. He was there and he really, really made sure that the sound, everything, the approach, the spirit in the room was right. We had these incredible string musicians there who didn’t know what the project was about and one came to me and says, “You know this reminds me, we used to record for Sarah like this.” And I was like, “Well this is dedicated to Sarah.” So once they realized that it became a party. And those four days, they were not long enough, because we had such a good time.
